The rates come from a bootstrap with far fewer draws than 50,000 and from schemes that resample 2018 to 2026 origins.

known_limits.title: The candidate against the calendar-aware GBM on quarter-end turns and year-ends
known_limits.ruling: Eleonora, 13 November 2026, option (a) on #1593: swapping in the calendar GBM is not supported, the quarter-end family keeps the frozen candidate, and no GBM or combination arm is opened.
known_limits.reading: Development data on days already seen, no verdict. d is the GBM minus the candidate on the same cells; 90% event-cluster intervals. Quarter-end turns, 22 events and 220 cells: the 90% band covers 0.586 for the candidate and 0.500 for the GBM (d -0.086 [-0.245, +0.077]); above q95 the candidate is exceeded 0.336 of the time and the GBM 0.255 (nominal 0.050); grid CRPS 3.512 against 4.141 (d +0.629 [-0.087, +1.413]); upper-tail twCRPS 2.136 against 2.422 (d +0.286 [-0.342, +0.982]). Year-ends, 8 events and 71 cells: 90% band 0.648 against 0.577 (d -0.070 [-0.141, +0.000]); grid CRPS 8.469 against 11.507 (d +3.038 [+0.525, +6.576]); upper-tail twCRPS 7.771 against 10.316 (d +2.545 [+0.065, +6.160]). On the quarter-end turns alone the score and coverage intervals hold zero; the candidate's band still covers far less than 90% there.
known_limits.caveat: The GBM's walks were made at the 16:00 instant, the candidate's at the 18:00 decision instant, so the GBM forecast with two hours less public information; that favours the candidate by an amount not measured. Several regime cells rest on fewer than five events, and the regimes are not tested against one another.
